limits: SIMULATED: every number on this feed comes from the simulator's stated noise model (hello.noise), not from a measurement.

A phone with no app cannot be ranged or identified: cold presence is a band of advertising devices per puck, never a position or an identity. Devices are not people: watches, earbuds and laptops advertise too, and some phones do not.

Cold count band: count = devices in the near and mid bands of one puck (signal at least -75 dBm: a few metres in line of sight; attributed to the puck's room); lower bound = half the count rounded down, but never fewer than the opt-in phones the feed places in that room (they advertise too); upper bound = the count plus half the far-band devices rounded up (some far devices are in the room behind furniture or bodies). Over-count causes: address rotation and several advertising sets per device. Under-count causes: idle phones that do not advertise, bodies. Entries from several pucks in one room hear the same devices: do not add them up.

A ring stays a ring: x and y are published only when the geometry is a fix. One puck gives a ring, two pucks two mirror-image candidates, three pucks not in a line (or one puck plus the phone's own bearing) one fix.
Bluetooth signal strength gives metres, not centimetres: a Bluetooth-only phone is a band or a room, never a precise point.

The twin prunes positions (outside the building, inside a wall, the wrong room for a line-of-sight link). This twin is a synthetic interior fitted to the real footprint, so pruning is only as good as its invented walls.
Floors come from the occupant's own report when given; otherwise the pucks' floor is assumed.
A phone not heard for 20 s is marked stale and its uncertainty grows by 0.25 m per second; it is dropped after 15 minutes.

Two pucks leave two mirror-image candidates. The twin removes one only when it is impossible; a possible candidate is dismissed only on stated evidence (the occupant's suite, or command's search room), and the phone then carries that assumption.
